seoTitle: AI & Software Solutions for Retail & e-commerce | Fruition
seoDescription: 16 retail & e-commerce use cases on monday.com, 2 with AI. See the process, boards, automations and integrations for each.
heading: Retail & e-commerce use cases
intro: Every use case comes from a real Fruition client engagement, with the client's name withheld. Select "See the build" for the process diagram, boards, automations and integrations.

faq.question: What do retail & e-commerce organisations build on monday.com with Fruition?
faq.answer: This page shows 16 retail & e-commerce use cases. The most common are CRM (9), integrations & migration (9), work & project management (8), most often for sales & CRM, marketing, customer service teams.

faq.question: How long does a retail & e-commerce monday.com build take?
faq.answer: The most common timeframe for a complete retail & e-commerce build is 6 to 12 months. Phased programs run longer, with later phases added once the core build is adopted.

faq.question: Which systems do retail & e-commerce builds integrate with?
faq.answer: The integrations that come up most often in retail & e-commerce use cases are Outlook, Make, Dealer management system, Office 365, SharePoint, Promotional Office.

faq.question: Does Fruition build AI agents for retail & e-commerce?
faq.answer: Yes. 2 of the retail & e-commerce use cases on this page include an AI step. Examples: AI email summaries on client threads.

useCases.title: Premium appliance distributor with a field sales team
useCases.summary: A field-based sales team managed visits, product displays, consignment stock and builder agreements across spreadsheets, email and personal knowledge, leaving sales leadership with no live view of activity or pipeline.
useCases.challenge: A field-based sales team managed visits, product displays, consignment stock and builder agreements across spreadsheets, email and personal knowledge, leaving sales leadership with no live view of activity or pipeline.
boards: Core CRM: leads, contacts, accounts (as hub) and deals with BDM/territory ownership
Weighted sales pipeline by rep, state and stage
BDM activity plan pre-populated weekly from call cycles
Store visit checklist auto-generated per visit and required before closing the visit
Displays and consignment stock tracking per retail account
Builder agreements/quotes with renewal dates
Internal requests board: requests to marketing, sales support and admin linked to account with approval workflow
Rep dashboard and head-of-sales dashboard (activity completion, weighted pipeline, accounts not visited in 30 days, renewals due)
automations: Visit started → auto-create store visit checklist; checklist must be completed to close visit
Calls captured from telephony auto-summarised and logged against the account
Email sequences: product/promo announcements, deal-stage follow-up, inactive-account re-engagement
useCases.outcome: A mobile-first CRM acting as the field-sales operating system, enforcing visit standards, tracking displays and consignment stock per account, and giving the sales head live activity and weighted-pipeline visibility.

process.title: Field sales store visits with enforced standards and AI

useCases.challenge: Leads were run from a shared inbox and spreadsheets with quotes in a separate system, so follow-ups and quote status were fragmented across email, Excel and other tools.

boards: Member marketing-request portal with conditional fields by request type and member-only ticket visibility

useCases.title: Multi-site motor vehicle dealership
useCases.summary: Sales staff double-entered customer and deal data between the CRM and the dealer management system, and service reminders were basic text messages with no link to whether a service had been booked.
useCases.challenge: Sales staff double-entered customer and deal data between the CRM and the dealer management system, and service reminders were basic text messages with no link to whether a service had been booked.
boards: CRM contacts and deals as sales front end, matched to dealer management system profiles
Upcoming-services board: one item per vehicle due for service, 12 months from last service
Deal status mirrored from dealer system for loyalty follow-up
automations: New contact in CRM → lookup in dealer system; match existing profile or create new, then create deal
Deal status change in dealer system (e.g. deposit received) → CRM opportunity stage updated
Service record in dealer system → future service item created; reminder SMS/email campaign runs until a booking syncs back and stops it
useCases.outcome: An API integration creating or matching customer profiles and deals in the dealer system from the CRM, syncing deal status back, and running service-reminder campaigns that stop once a service is booked.

process.title: CRM synced with dealer system and service reminders
